reader_question: How many of every 100 workers belong to a union?
grade_line: Documented: the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ count of union members, as the atlas records it
title: One in ten U.S. wage and salary workers belonged to a union in 2025.
measure_line: Union members as a share of employed wage and salary workers, 2025 annual average, drawn as people out of 100, United States
notes: In 1983, 20.1 percent of wage and salary workers belonged to a union. In 2025, 5.9 percent of workers in the private sector did and 32.9 percent in the public sector, 14.7 million members in all.
The Bureau says the 2025 average, which leaves out October, is not strictly comparable with other years’ averages.
chart_notes: Each square stands for one worker in 100: the 10 union members are filled, in the text’s ink, and the 90 others are open.
alt: A grid of 100 squares, one for each worker in 100. The first row of 10 is filled for union members in 2025, and the other 90 are open.
